title.en: John Byro, Uncle Khosrove and the meeting on the road

hook.en: Imagine eating breakfast while the man whose horse you secretly ride sits at your table complaining that it was stolen.

objectives.en: Describe John Byro's visit and Uncle Khosrove's reaction
Explain why Byro does not accuse the boys
Recognise the irony and humour of the roadside meeting

narration.en: Imagine eating breakfast while the man whose horse you secretly ride sits at your table complaining that it was stolen.

body.en: John Byro visits Aram's house and sadly tells how his white horse was stolen some time ago, so that his surrey is of no use to him. Uncle Khosrove, who is present, loses patience and tells him it is no great harm and to stop worrying. Aram hears all this and understands at once whose horse they have.

points.en: Byro: the stolen horse, a useless surrey
Uncle Khosrove: brushes the loss aside
Aram realises the horse is Byro's

narration.en: John Byro visits Aram's house and sadly tells how his white horse was stolen some time ago, so that his surrey is of no use to him. Uncle Khosrove, who is present, loses patience and tells him it is no great harm and to stop worrying. Aram hears all this and understands at once whose horse they have.
This flowchart shows how Byro's trust turns the story towards its ending.

say.en: Byro visits and tells the family his horse was stolen.
Uncle Khosrove brushes his loss aside.
Aram realises their horse is Byro's.
On the road, Byro sees the boys on his horse.
He chooses to trust the family's honest name.
That trust works on the boys' conscience.

title.en: The plot from barn to farm

narration.en: The main events of the story, retold in our own words. Put them in order.
narration.kn: ಘಟನೆಗಳನ್ನು ನಮ್ಮ ಮಾತುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾರ್ಡ್‌ಗಳಾಗಿ ನೀಡಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಯಾದ ಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಜೋಡಿಸಿ.

prompt.en: Put the events of the story in order.

steps.en: Mourad wakes Aram at dawn with the white horse
The cousins ride together through the countryside
Aram rides alone and is thrown
Mourad brings the horse back and they hide it
John Byro visits and tells of his stolen horse
Uncle Khosrove tells him not to worry
The boys meet Byro on a country road
Byro trusts the family's honesty and lets them go
The boys return the horse to Byro's vineyard
Byro reports the horse came back better than before

explanation.en: The meeting on the road is the turning point: Byro's trust makes the boys return the horse.

body.en: Soon after, the boys ride straight into John Byro on a country road. Byro studies the horse closely and says it looks just like his, but he would swear so only if he did not know their parents, because the family is famous for honesty. He wishes them good day and lets them go.

points.en: Trust in the family overrides his eyes
Irony: the honest family's sons are riding his horse

narration.en: Soon after, the boys ride straight into John Byro on a country road. Byro studies the horse closely and says it looks just like his, but he would swear so only if he did not know their parents, because the family is famous for honesty. He wishes them good day and lets them go.

problem.en: Why did John Byro not accuse the boys of stealing his horse when he met them?

steps.en: Byro recognised the horse as his.
But he knew the boys' family and its reputation for honesty.
So he chose trust over suspicion and let them go.

answer.en: Although the horse looked exactly like his, Byro knew the boys' parents and their family's fame for honesty. He chose to trust that reputation rather than accuse the boys, and simply let them ride on.

Meeting the boys on the road, Byro recognises the horse but trusts the family's honesty.
The scene is ironic and gently comic.
